posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
There's one thing I'm concerned about this whole contest.

Most of the time in comics when two main characters throw down, theres times that the most common sense answer won't be the outcome. We'll use two heroes in this example that each have a comic book line, yet hero A has a higher 'power level' than hero B.

A character's popularity usually is a large factor, normally tipping the scale in their favor, especially if a fan vote is held(Like Marvel vs DC in the 90's).

The writer also could throw a curve-ball, either having some sort of extenuating circumstance that severly tips the scales in hero B's favor.

Heck, the book where the fight takes place is a major factor as well!

Long story short, I don't want to send my well thought out bracket guesses in and have them all correct EXCEPT for the one in a trillion chance that Ermine somehow single-handedly defeats Progeny(just an example).

Champion: Legacy, come on guys Iron Legacy is the hardest villain in the game, and all he is is Legacy not holding back. Not to mention popularity power if we are going off of that.

Tech: Writhe, ironically not for his Tech but for his portal to hell power and intangibility which basically makes him untouchable.

Argent Adept: Sure the other mystics may know more about what they're doing, but Argent Adept can just start jamming on the saxophone and undo the world if he wanted to.

Conqueror: Progeny, duh.

Cunning: Baron Blade, also duh.

Eldritch: Lifeline, this was a tough call, but seeing as how he oneshotted Gloomweaver once, I'll bet he can do it again.

Bruiser: Bugbear, he's just too strong.

Final Victory: Progeny, it is very strong.

There are so many heroes I just don't know the parameters of though. D:

Is Writhe tangible? If so, I'm pretty sure he could lose to Absolute Zero. But if not, I don't know how AZ could touch him.

Are Biomancer's Fleshchildren capable of being raised as zombies and used against him?

Is Sgt. Steel by himself, or does he get all his Agent buddies to back him up?

Are these "you must fight!" fights, or is sitting down and talking acceptable? What happens when Medico has to fight his daughter? What do Benchmark or Kaargra Warfang even do? I mean, I'm glad we're getting some info on what, exactly, the Cosmic Contest is, I think I'd just rather have these questions being asked after we've heard all the character episodes and seen all the decks in play. :/

That said, I thought the hardest starting fight was Wraith vs. Fixer. They just seem really evenly matched physically, and it's all about planning vs. experience. And maybe Driving Mantising a few knives back where they came from.

posts.name: Yoshi348
posts.cooked:
I definitely went into this with a "this is a big comic crossover story, how would the writers write this" mindset. That said there's a lot of different factors that brings into play that makes decisions all over the place tough.

In the champion tier Legacy just goes to town, he's Legacy, man! Plus the upper half where he hangs out is just full of people who don't really have a specific angle to work against him or anything, which is probably what you're going to need to deal with him. Bottom half was really hard to figure out; CC and Tempest are both super versatile, while Void Guard Mainstay vs. Tachyon isn't just a brain vs. brawn match since Mainstay's got a good head on his shoulders, plus without any of the Void Guard decks I don't really have a handle on their real power set. Then I realised that if I broke the ties right I'd get TEMPEST VS TACHYON GRUDGE MATCH SUNDAY SUNDAY SUNDAY so in that went.

Other highlights: I actually had Benchmark get past AZ cause they were really pushing his character plus AZ gets all the hard knocks. Parse being the ultimate winner of this tier wasn't what I expected going in but all the parts made sense to me. Martial tier head towards Setback vs. Expatriette because that's not just comics drama that's exactly what Setback's luck would do; fluke a victory at the last minute over K.N.Y.F.E. and then he'd learn who he was fighting next. I assume Progeny is just his head because well… that's all he is at this point and not just his head would win the tournament twice over without breaking a sweat. I had him bouncing to Legacy so we can get Yet Another Baron Blade vs. Legacy fight (though it didn't really consider aiming towards this until way too late). I almost had Blade win so that there would be hero vs. villian in the finals with my bracket but I realized that for Blade that would be a shining moment important enough to be part of his story, so no go there.
